examFormat.mix: Multiple choice, definition-heavy. A classmate's confirmed intel lists ~16 exact topics — those are the ★ items below and they come FIRST.
examFormat.notes: Every ★ item was named by a classmate who saw the exam. Definitions here include an example, because the exam asks you to recognize the concept in a scenario.

verifiedPatterns.pattern: Definition-recognition MCQ: a term is described in a scenario and you pick the name (cardinality, taxonomy, crowdsourcing, conversion rate, community of practice, knowledge management)

NOT/EXCEPT questions — 'which is NOT a responsibility of project management', 'what will an LMS NOT do', 'what is NOT part of ETL'. Read the stem twice; the odd one out is usually the REPORTING/analysis step.
Compare-the-pair: analog vs digital · thin vs thick client · server-centric vs client-centric · data warehouse vs data mart · byte→KB→MB→GB→TB
Two answers were leaked outright: Q1 = server-centric, Q2 = thin client

topics.name: Confirmed exam intel (answer these first)
topics.why: A classmate listed the exact topics on the test. Every ★ item traces to that email — highest-value 15 minutes of study.

topics.name: Databases, cardinality & SQL
topics.why: Cardinality is named TWICE in the intel ('how tables talk to each other'). Keys, normalization, ETL all live here.

topics.name: Hardware, networks & storage units
topics.why: Byte→ZB table is a confirmed question; analog vs digital and thin client are confirmed answers.

topics.name: Business intelligence, ETL & analytics
topics.why: ETL NOT-question confirmed; BI vs analytics, OLAP, warehouse vs mart, 3 analytics types.

topics.name: Project management & risk
topics.why: Critical path + risk management + the 'NOT a PM responsibility' free question are all confirmed.

topics.name: Knowledge management & data visualization
topics.why: Community of practice, taxonomy, crowdsourcing, LMS, conversion rate, viz principles — all confirmed MCQ fodder.

formulas.name: ★ Storage units — the ladder
formulas.vars: byte = bits needed for ONE character
formulas.when: Confirmed question — 'know the difference between bytes, gigabyte, terabyte'
formulas.trap: Each step is 1,024 (2¹⁰), NOT 1,000 — and the order is B→KB→MB→GB→TB→PB→EB→ZB

formulas.name: ★ Cardinality — how tables talk
formulas.vars: the LINES on a relationship diagram
formulas.when: Named twice in the intel — the single most likely question
formulas.trap: Cardinality is the NUMBER of links in the relationship, not the key itself. The crow's-foot LINES are the cardinality.
formulas.ex: A student has ONE advisor, an advisor advises MANY students → 1:M. A department has many advisors and an advisor serves many departments → M:N

formulas.name: ★ Critical path (project time mgmt)
formulas.formula: critical path = the LONGEST path of dependent tasks through the project
formulas.trap: It is the LONGEST duration path, not the shortest or the cheapest — and any delay on it delays the WHOLE project
formulas.ex: A(3d)→B(5d)→D(2d) = 10 days vs A(3d)→C(1d)→D(2d) = 6 days → critical path is A-B-D; slipping B one day slips the project one day

formulas.name: ★ ETL — Extract, Transform, Load
formulas.when: Confirmed 'what is NOT part of ETL' question
formulas.trap: Creating meaningful REPORTS is NOT part of ETL — that's the reporting layer. Also: NEVER use Transform to manipulate report data (it breaks warehouse integrity).
formulas.ex: Extract sales from POS DB · Transform = cleanse + normalize + translate codes · Load = organize, relate, catalog with metadata

formulas.name: SQL skeleton
formulas.formula: SELECT fields FROM tables WHERE conditions ORDER BY field
formulas.vars: SELECT=what to see · FROM=source tables · WHERE=conditions + joins · AND/OR=combine · ORDER BY=sort
formulas.trap: The '=' in WHERE both filters AND establishes the table relationship (or use JOIN)
formulas.ex: SELECT Name, Dept FROM Employee, Department WHERE Employee.DeptID = Department.DeptID ORDER BY Name

formulas.name: Key fields
formulas.formula: Primary Key (unique in THIS table) → Foreign Key (that PK used in ANOTHER table)
formulas.vars: key field = uniquely identifies a record
formulas.trap: The foreign key lives in the SECOND table as the look-up back to the original — don't reverse it
formulas.ex: Employee.EmpID is the PK; in Timesheet, EmpID is the FK pointing back to Employee

concepts.def: A device that does almost NO processing itself — it relies on the server for applications, storage and computing power; mostly just displays the result. (Confirmed exam ANSWER #2.)
An architecture where processing and data live on the SERVER rather than the user's machine. (Confirmed exam ANSWER #1.)

Analog = continuous physical WAVES (infinitely variable). Digital = discrete BINARY numbers, 0s and 1s. Example: a vinyl record groove (analog) vs an MP3 file (digital); a dimmer knob vs a light switch.

Malware/hardware that RECORDS EVERY KEYSTROKE, so it captures everyone's passwords as they type them. The USB-stick version that auto-types payloads when plugged in is called a rubber ducky. Example: a USB dongle left in a lab PC harvesting logins all week.

Identifying, assessing and PRIORITIZING project risks, then planning responses (avoid / mitigate / transfer / accept) and monitoring them. Example: key developer might quit → mitigate by documenting and cross-training.

A GROUP OF PEOPLE who share a craft or profession and learn from each other by interacting regularly — informal, voluntary, knowledge-sharing. Example: all the Tableau users across different departments meeting monthly to swap dashboard tricks.
The PERCENTAGE OF VISITORS who take the desired action — i.e. people converting into users/customers on your site. Example: 5,000 visitors, 250 sign up → 5% conversion rate.

Obtaining ideas, content, or work by soliciting contributions from a LARGE OPEN GROUP of people (usually online) instead of from employees or a vendor. Example: Wikipedia articles, Waze traffic reports, a logo contest on 99designs.

Firm-wide effort to COLLECT, STORE, DISTRIBUTE and APPLY digital content and knowledge so expertise isn't lost. Includes enterprise KM systems and knowledge work systems (KWS) for engineers/scientists. Example: an internal wiki of solved support tickets.

A CLASSIFICATION SCHEME — a hierarchical way of organizing and naming things into categories so they can be found. Example: a product catalog organized Electronics → Computers → Laptops; or the folder/tag hierarchy in a document system.

Software to DELIVER, TRACK and ADMINISTER training/courses — hosts content, enrolls learners, records completion and scores. Example: eLearning, Blackboard, Canvas. Watch the NOT-question: an LMS does not write your course content, run payroll, or manage the company's operational databases.
Data = streams of RAW FACTS. Information = data shaped into a MEANINGFUL FORM. Example: '78, 92, 85' is data; 'class average = 85' is information.
Database → Table (file) → Row (record) → Column (field) → characters. Entity = the person/place/thing you store info about; Attribute (metadata) = a characteristic describing it.
Program to CREATE, PROCESS and ADMINISTER a database; centralizes data and controls redundancy so one database serves many applications. A relational DBMS represents data as two-dimensional tables.
Streamlining complex data groupings to MINIMIZE REDUNDANCY and remove awkward many-to-many relationships. Example: splitting one bloated Employee sheet into Employee + Department tables.
RDBMS rules ensuring relationships between tables stay CONSISTENT — you can't point a foreign key at a row that doesn't exist.
In the normalized example the Employee table is the FACT table (the measured events) and the Department table is the DIMENSION table (descriptive context).

Warehouse = current + historical data from MANY operational systems, consolidated enterprise-wide, and CANNOT be altered. Data mart = a SUBSET focused on one subject or line of business. Example: enterprise warehouse vs the Marketing-only mart.
Massive UNSTRUCTURED/semi-structured datasets (web traffic, social media, sensors) too large for a typical DBMS — petabytes/exabytes; needs new tools and reveals more patterns.

Hadoop = distributed parallel processing across cheap computers. In-memory computing = uses RAM instead of disk, cutting hours to seconds. Analytic platforms = high-speed relational + non-relational systems for big datasets.
Rapid ONLINE answers over many dimensions, insulated from operational processing. Example: a pivot table slicing sales by region × quarter × product.
Data mining = find hidden patterns and relationships in datasets. Text mining = extract key elements from UNSTRUCTURED text. Web mining = discovery from web content, structure and usage.

Descriptive = describe performance from established data (financial reports, statistics). Predictive = predict future trends from past performance (credit scoring, sales projections). Prescriptive = analyze current situation to recommend action (optimization, simulation).
Strategic = UNSTRUCTURED, top level, overall direction and goals. Tactical = SEMI-structured, midlevel, how to achieve the strategy. Operational = STRUCTURED, day-to-day, closest to the customer.
Objective = data-driven, quantitative, measurable (numbers, structured, analytical). Subjective = qualitative, perception and intuition (unstructured, opinion, exploratory).

BI = the INFRASTRUCTURE for collecting, storing and analyzing business data (databases, warehouses, marts). Business analytics = the TOOLS AND TECHNIQUES applied to it (OLAP, statistics, models, data mining).
Support SEMI-STRUCTURED decisions with mathematical/analytical models — 'what-if' analysis, sensitivity analysis, backward sensitivity, multidimensional/OLAP.

concepts.term: Expert system vs neural network vs genetic algorithm
concepts.def: Expert system = captures tacit knowledge as RULES (knowledge base + inference engine). Neural network = learns BY EXAMPLE. Genetic algorithm = searches a huge solution space with a DNA-like approach. Case-based reasoning = reuses past cases. Fuzzy logic = handles imprecision.
Software that searches external sources for solutions on your behalf. Example: Siri, Priceline.com.
Project = a planned undertaking with a BEGINNING AND END producing a definite result. Program = an interrelated COLLECTION of projects.
30–40% of IT projects exceed schedule/budget or fail to perform as specified. Failure types: missing essential business requirements, no organizational benefit, poor UI, inaccurate/inconsistent data.

Corporate strategic planning group (firm strategy) → IS steering committee (approves plans across divisions) → project management group (oversees specific projects) → project team (one system project).

A network is TWO OR MORE connected computers. Components: client + server, NICs, connection medium, network OS, hubs/switches/routers. LAN = local area; WAN = wide area. SDN = switch/router functions run by a central program.
Every device gets an IP address (32-bit, e.g. 207.46.250.119). DNS converts IP addresses to domain names in a hierarchical structure with top-level domains.

'Virtual' = appears to exist but does not. VPN client ENCRYPTS the message, wraps it with the VPN server's address, sends it over the Internet; the gateway strips the address, DECRYPTS it and delivers plain text inside the LAN.

Commodity = a widely available good whose availability lowers cost and shrinks margins so price dominates. The cloud 'commoditizes' key infrastructure to lower overall cost — enabled by better speed and security.

Advantages: cost savings, employee satisfaction, less training, higher productivity, lower support cost. Disadvantages: data loss/damage, loss of control, compatibility problems, infection risk, greater support cost. (Support cost appears on BOTH sides — a classic trick.)
3G ≈ 144 Kbps (email, browsing). 4G up to 100 Mbps (Internet video), LTE/WiMax. 5G = 10–20× faster downloads, better spectrum use, more devices. CDMA = US only; GSM = rest of world (AT&T, T-Mobile).
Desktop (individual) · Server (sharing) · Reader (read files) · Online (BI in the cloud) · Public (free, publishes online).
Data connection/preparation → data exploration → data VISUALIZATION (the heart) → data analysis → data storytelling (interactive dashboards and stories).
Live = queries the source directly and stays current. Extract = a snapshot pulled into Tableau, faster but as of the extract time.
Location analytics = business insight from the GEOGRAPHIC component of data (phones, sensors, map data). GIS ties location data to maps. Example: local government computing disaster response times.
Business activity monitoring using data generated by SENSORS — the Internet of Things creating huge real-time streams; descriptive and/or prescriptive in nature.

tables.title: ★ ETL — and what is NOT in it

traps.text: ★ "Creating meaningful reports is part of ETL" is FALSE — ETL is Extract, Transform, Load only; reporting is a separate layer. The intel says this exact NOT-question is on the exam.
★ Using the Transform step to manipulate REPORT data is WRONG — it destroys data-warehouse integrity. Transform is for cleansing/normalizing on the way IN.
★ "Cardinality means the primary key" is FALSE — cardinality is the measure of the NUMBER OF LINKS in a relationship (1:1, 1:M, M:N); it's what the connecting LINES on the diagram show.
★ "A kilobyte is 1,000 bytes" is FALSE — it's 1,024 (2¹⁰). Every rung of the ladder multiplies by 1,024, not 1,000.
★ "Analog means old and digital means new" is WRONG — the real difference is CONTINUOUS WAVES (analog) vs DISCRETE BINARY 0s and 1s (digital).
★ "A thin client does the processing locally" is FALSE — the thin client offloads processing to the SERVER; that's what makes it thin.
★ "The critical path is the shortest route through the project" is FALSE — it is the LONGEST chain of dependent tasks, and it has zero slack.
"An LMS builds your course content and runs the business's databases" is FALSE — an LMS delivers, tracks and administers training; authoring content and operational data management are NOT its job.
"A data mart holds everything the warehouse holds" is FALSE — a mart is a SUBSET focused on a single subject or line of business.
"Strategic decisions are structured" is FALSE — strategic = UNSTRUCTURED, tactical = semi-structured, operational = structured. The exam loves flipping these.
"Data and information mean the same thing" is FALSE — data is raw facts; information is data shaped into meaningful form.
"Project management in IT is only an IT responsibility" is FALSE — implementation projects must NEVER be considered solely IT projects, even though PM is a core IT competency.
"Predictive analytics recommends the best action" is FALSE — that's PRESCRIPTIVE (optimization, simulation). Predictive forecasts what is likely to happen.
"BI and business analytics are the same" is FALSE — BI is the infrastructure (warehouses, marts); analytics is the toolset applied to it (OLAP, mining, models).
"A foreign key must be unique in its own table" is FALSE — the PRIMARY key is unique; the foreign key repeats as a look-up to the other table.
"BYOD always reduces support costs" is FALSE — the slide lists reduced support costs as an advantage AND greater support costs as a disadvantage; read which side the question is asking about.

questions.q: ★ Confirmed answer #1 → server-centric
★ Confirmed answer #2 → thin client
★ The lines showing relationships between tables are called…? → cardinality

★ Which is NOT a responsibility of project management in IT? → the intel calls this a 'free question' — pick the option that is an operational/technical task, not planning, scope, time, cost, quality, risk or resources
★ What is NOT part of an ETL process? → creating meaningful reports
★ What will a typical LMS NOT do? → author your content / run operational business databases (it delivers, tracks and administers training)
★ Difference between analog and digital? → analog = continuous physical waves; digital = discrete binary 0s and 1s
★ What is a critical path? → the longest chain of dependent tasks; delay on it delays the whole project
★ What unlocks everyone's password by recording keystrokes, also called a rubber ducky? → a keylogger
★ Order these: byte, gigabyte, terabyte, megabyte, kilobyte → B < KB < MB < GB < TB (×1,024 each)
★ A group who share a profession and learn from each other by interacting regularly → community of practice
★ Percentage of site visitors who become users → conversion rate
★ Getting ideas or work from a large open online group → crowdsourcing
★ Collecting, storing, distributing and applying firm knowledge → knowledge management
★ A hierarchical classification scheme for organizing things → taxonomy
★ Identifying, prioritizing and planning responses to project threats → risk management
A student has one advisor; an advisor has many students. What cardinality? → one-to-many (1:M)
Which key appears in a second table as a look-up back to the first? → foreign key
Streamlining data to minimize redundancy and remove many-to-many relationships → normalization
Which stores current AND historical data from many systems and cannot be altered? → data warehouse (a mart is a subset)
Credit scoring and sales projections are examples of which analytics? → predictive
Optimization and simulation are examples of which analytics? → prescriptive
Which decision type is typically unstructured and sets overall direction? → strategic
Which BI tool gives rapid multidimensional answers insulated from operational processing? → OLAP
Which mining type extracts key elements from unstructured text? → text mining
Which AI technique learns by example? → neural networks (expert systems use rules; genetic algorithms search huge solution spaces)
Distributed parallel processing of big data across inexpensive computers → Hadoop
Which uses RAM instead of disk to cut processing from hours to seconds? → in-memory computing
T/F: A project is an interrelated collection of programs. → FALSE — a PROGRAM is an interrelated collection of PROJECTS
What percentage of IT projects are runaway projects? → 30–40%
Which encrypts a message, wraps it for a gateway, then decrypts it inside the LAN? → VPN
What converts IP addresses to domain names? → DNS
Which Tableau product is free and publishes interactive data online? → Tableau Public
What is the 'heart' of what Tableau does? → data visualization
